label: organizations confirmed breached by name
detail: Still none by name. Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 now describes one intrusion at an unnamed government entity in Europe: within two hours of exploitation an attacker it judges to be an AI agent had password hashes and multi-factor secrets and was trying for domain admin. The victim, the data source and the outcome are not stated; TechCrunch calls it a confirmed compromise. The Trail of Bits post TechCrunch also cites, read on Oct 25, describes the firm's own exploit reaching production grade, not a breach. Sophos retracted its one earlier claim.

label: exploit attempts seen by Cloudflare
detail: Tens of thousands within 45 minutes of disclosure, millions by Oct 22. Some attempts try to enlist servers into a Mirai botnet variant (Potassium); no infection count has been published.

label: UK government digital services confirmed unavailable
detail: Plus four partially unavailable, mostly precautionary. The NCSC has issued about 50,000 warnings.

label: PHP services Censys counts on affected versions
detail: As of Oct 22, against about 1 million on a fixed release; Censys separately assesses 34.4 million services on 3.1 million hosts as vulnerable. Versions before 8.2 will never get an official fix.

label: of 2.6M exposed PHP hosts VulnCheck rates vulnerable or likely vulnerable
detail: 2,608,039 internet-facing hosts as of Oct 23: 1,474,985 advertise a version below the fixed build, 1,133,000 hide their version, 700,000+ run PHP 3.x to 7.3. Qualys separately saw 199,000 instances patched in the first 12 hours and counts about 110 million on end-of-life versions.

label: on CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
detail: The feed, opened directly at 06:40 ET Oct 25 (and three times on Oct 24): catalog version 2026.10.23, released Oct 23 at 19:30 UTC, 1,756 entries, none of the three PHP CVEs; the Oct 23 additions were Arista VeloCloud and Collabora Online. No federal emergency directive reported. A listing is CISA's formal verdict that exploitation is real.
